errors.message_template: use of moved value: `%0`
errors.cause: An `_Owned` pointer was used after its ownership was transferred (moved) to another variable or consumed by a function call. Once ownership moves, the source variable becomes invalid and cannot be read, dereferenced, or passed to another function. The compiler tracks these moves and flags any subsequent use of the invalidated variable.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_use_moved]

errors.message_template: use of partially moved value: `%0`, %1 moved
errors.cause: A struct or composite value containing `_Owned` pointer fields was used after one or more (but not all) of its `_Owned` fields had their ownership moved out. The struct is in a partially valid state: some fields are still owned while others have been invalidated. Using the struct as a whole is not permitted because the moved fields are no longer valid.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_use_partially_moved]

errors.message_template: use of all moved value: `%0`
errors.cause: A struct or composite value was used after all of its `_Owned` fields had their ownership moved out individually. The entire struct is now invalid because every owned field has been transferred elsewhere. This is distinct from a simple move of the struct itself -- here each field was moved separately, leaving the struct completely drained.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_use_all_moved]

errors.message_template: use of uninitialized value: `%0`
errors.cause: An `_Owned` pointer variable was used before any value was assigned to it. Unlike regular C pointers where reading an uninitialized variable is merely undefined behavior, BSC treats this as a hard error for `_Owned` pointers. The compiler requires every `_Owned` variable to be definitively initialized before use to prevent double-free or use-after-free scenarios.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_use_uninit]

errors.message_template: use of possibly uninitialized value: `%0`
errors.cause: An `_Owned` pointer was used on a code path where it might not have been initialized. This typically happens when the variable is initialized inside a conditional branch but used unconditionally afterward. The compiler performs flow-sensitive analysis and detects that at least one execution path reaches the use without a prior initialization.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_use_possibly_uninit]

errors.message_template: assign to _Owned value: `%0`
errors.cause: A new value was assigned to an `_Owned` pointer that already owns allocated memory. This would silently leak the previously owned memory because the old pointer value is overwritten without being freed first. BSC requires that the current ownership be released (via `free_owned` or a move) before a new value can be assigned.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_owned]

errors.message_template: assign to partially moved value: `%0`, %1 moved
errors.cause: A whole-struct assignment was attempted on an `_Owned` struct where some fields have been moved out but others still hold ownership. Overwriting the entire struct would leak the memory owned by the fields that were not moved. The compiler requires that the struct be in a consistent state (either fully owned or fully moved/freed) before a whole-struct assignment.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_partially_moved]

errors.message_template: assign to possibly partially moved value: `%0`, %1 possibly moved
errors.cause: A whole-struct assignment was attempted on an `_Owned` struct where some fields may or may not have been moved out depending on the control flow. The compiler cannot guarantee that the struct is in a consistent state at the assignment point, because some execution paths move a field while others do not. This ambiguity makes it impossible to determine whether the assignment would leak memory.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_possibly_partially_moved]

errors.message_template: assign to all moved value: `%0`
errors.cause: A whole-struct assignment was attempted on an `_Owned` struct where all `_Owned` fields have been individually moved out. While this might seem safe (no memory would leak), BSC still flags this because the struct was drained field-by-field rather than moved as a whole unit. The compiler treats an all-moved struct as being in an invalid state that requires explicit reinitialization through field-by-field assignment rather than whole-struct assignment.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_all_moved]

errors.message_template: assign to part of uninitialized value: `%0`
errors.cause: An assignment was made to a field of an `_Owned` struct that has not been initialized at all. BSC requires that the struct variable itself be in a known state before individual fields can be assigned. Assigning to a single field of a completely uninitialized struct leaves other fields in an indeterminate state, which can lead to double-free or leak issues when the struct goes out of scope.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_field_uninit]

errors.message_template: assign to part of _Owned value: `%0`
errors.cause: An assignment was made to a field of an `_Owned` struct when that field already holds an owned value. Overwriting the field would leak the memory it currently owns. Just as with reassigning a top-level `_Owned` pointer, BSC requires the field's current value to be freed or moved before a new value can be assigned to it.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_field_owned]

errors.message_template: assign to part of moved value: `%0`
errors.cause: An assignment was made to a field of an `_Owned` struct whose ownership has been moved as a whole. Once the entire struct has been moved to another variable or consumed by a function, the original variable is invalid. Assigning to a field of a moved struct is not permitted because the struct itself no longer exists as a valid entity in the current scope.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_field_moved]

errors.message_template: assign to subfield _Owned value: `%0`, %1 _Owned
errors.cause: An assignment was attempted to a nested field (subfield) of an `_Owned` struct where the subfield or its parent still holds an owned value. This is the nested variant of BSC-E0111: when structs contain other structs with `_Owned` fields, the ownership tracking extends transitively. Overwriting a subfield that still owns memory would leak that memory.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_assign_field_subfield_owned]

errors.message_template: invalid cast to `void * _Owned` of moved or uninitialized value: `%0`
errors.cause: A cast to `void *_Owned` was attempted on a variable whose ownership has already been moved or that was never initialized. Casting a moved or uninitialized pointer to `void *_Owned` would create a dangling owned pointer, because the underlying memory is either owned elsewhere or does not exist. This would lead to double-free or use-after-free bugs.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_cast_moved]

errors.message_template: invalid cast to `void * _Owned` of _Owned value: `%0`
errors.cause: A cast to `void *_Owned` was attempted on a variable that currently owns memory. This cast would create a second `_Owned` reference to the same memory, violating the single-ownership invariant. The original variable would still appear to own the memory, leading to potential double-free when both the original and the cast result are freed.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_cast_owned]

errors.message_template: invalid cast to `void * _Owned` of uninit value: `%0`
errors.cause: A cast to `void *_Owned` was attempted on a variable that has never been initialized. The pointer contains an indeterminate value, and casting it to `void *_Owned` would create an owned pointer pointing to arbitrary memory. Any subsequent operation on this pointer (dereference, free) would cause undefined behavior.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_cast_uninit]

errors.message_template: invalid cast to `void * _Owned` of not all moved value: `%0`, %1 _Owned
errors.cause: A cast to `void *_Owned` was attempted on an `_Owned` struct pointer where some fields have been moved but others still hold ownership. Casting the struct pointer to `void *_Owned` in this inconsistent state is not permitted because it is unclear whether the cast should transfer ownership of the remaining fields. The struct must be in a fully owned or fully moved state for a safe cast.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_cast_subfield_owned]

errors.message_template: memory leak of value: `%0`
errors.cause: An `_Owned` pointer variable goes out of scope while still owning heap memory. BSC requires that all `_Owned` pointers be either freed or moved before the end of their scope. If the pointer is not explicitly handled, the allocated memory is leaked. This is one of the most fundamental ownership errors and directly corresponds to a memory leak bug.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_memory_leak]

errors.message_template: field memory leak of value: `%0`, %1 leak
errors.cause: An `_Owned` struct goes out of scope while one or more of its `_Owned` fields still own heap memory. Even if the struct itself was handled (e.g., some fields were moved), the remaining fields still hold allocations that are not freed. Each `_Owned` field in a struct must be individually freed or moved before the struct goes out of scope.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_memory_leak_field]

errors.message_template: partially moved _Owned struct:`%0` at scope end, %1 moved
errors.cause: An `_Owned` struct reached the end of its scope in a partially moved state: some fields had their ownership transferred while others were not freed or moved. This is related to but distinct from BSC-E0119. The compiler specifically flags that the struct is in an inconsistent state at scope end, meaning neither a full free nor a full move was performed. The unmoved fields leak and the struct is left in an invalid intermediate state.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_owned_struct_patially_moved]

errors.message_template: destructor for`%0` incorrect, %1 of _Owned type and needs to be handled manually
errors.cause: The destructor defined for an `_Owned` struct does not properly handle all of the struct's `_Owned` fields. BSC verifies that destructors free or move every `_Owned` field in the struct. If any `_Owned` field is not explicitly handled within the destructor body, the compiler reports this error because those fields would leak when the destructor is called.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_ownership_owned_struct_not_properly_freed]

errors.message_template: %0 cannot be qualified by '_Owned'
errors.cause: The `_Owned` qualifier was applied to a declaration that does not support ownership semantics. Not all declarations can be qualified with `_Owned`. For example, function declarations, typedef names, or certain storage classes may not be compatible with ownership tracking. The `_Owned` qualifier is only meaningful on pointer types that represent heap-allocated memory.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_decl]

example.bad_code:
_Owned int x = 42;           // error: x cannot be qualified by '_Owned'
_Owned void func(void);      // error: func cannot be qualified by '_Owned'

errors.message_template: %select{type of %2 cannot qualified by '%1' |type of %2 cannot qualified by '%1', %3 contains '%1' type |type of %2 cannot qualified by '%1'(even indirectly), %3 contains '%1' type}0
errors.cause: The compiler detected that a type is being qualified with `_Owned` (or contains `_Owned` indirectly through nested types) in a context where this is not allowed. BSC performs deep type inspection and tracks `_Owned` qualifiers through nested structs, typedefs, and pointer chains. If an `_Owned` type appears at a nesting level where ownership cannot be properly tracked, this error is emitted. The three message variants correspond to: direct qualification error, direct containment of `_Owned`, and indirect (transitive) containment of `_Owned`.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_inderictOwned_type_check]

errors.message_template: cannot cast %0 to %1
errors.cause: A function pointer cast was attempted between two function pointer types that have incompatible `_Owned` qualifiers in their parameter or return types. Function pointer casts that change ownership semantics are dangerous because the caller and callee would disagree about who owns the memory. For example, casting a function that takes a non-owned pointer to one that takes an `_Owned` pointer could lead to double-free or leak.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_funcPtr_incompatible]

errors.message_template: incompatible _Owned types, cannot cast %0 to %1
errors.cause: A cast was attempted between two pointer types with incompatible `_Owned` qualifications. BSC enforces that casts preserve ownership semantics: you cannot cast a non-owned pointer to an `_Owned` pointer (which would fabricate ownership) or cast an `_Owned` pointer to a non-owned pointer (which would silently discard ownership and leak memory). Only compatible ownership-preserving casts are allowed.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_qualcheck_incompatible]

errors.message_template: memory leak because temporary variable '%0' is _Owned or indirect _Owned type, please fix it
errors.cause: A temporary (unnamed or short-lived) variable of `_Owned` type or a type that indirectly contains `_Owned` fields was created but its result was not captured. Since temporary values are destroyed at the end of the full expression, any `_Owned` memory they hold would be leaked. BSC detects this pattern and requires that the result of expressions producing `_Owned` types be stored in a named variable so the ownership can be properly managed.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_temporary_memLeak]

errors.message_template: type of %1 cannot be qualified by '%0'
errors.cause: The `_Owned` qualifier was applied to a non-pointer type. The `_Owned` qualifier is only meaningful on pointer types because it indicates that the pointer is responsible for the lifetime of the heap memory it points to. Applying `_Owned` to an integer, float, struct (non-pointer), or other non-pointer type has no meaningful ownership semantics and is rejected by the compiler.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_qualifier_non_pointer]

errors.message_template: cannot combine '_Owned' and '_Borrow' qualifiers on the same type
errors.cause: Both `_Owned` and `_Borrow` qualifiers were applied to the same type. These qualifiers are mutually exclusive: `_Owned` means the pointer owns its memory and is responsible for freeing it, while `_Borrow` means the pointer is a temporary, non-owning reference to memory owned elsewhere. A pointer cannot simultaneously own and not own the memory it points to.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_and_borrow_conflict]

errors.message_template: invalid operands to binary expression (%0 and %1)
errors.cause: A binary operator (such as `+`, `-`, `<`, `>`, `==`) was applied to one or more `_Owned` pointer operands. BSC does not allow arithmetic or comparison operations on `_Owned` pointers because these operations could produce interior pointers that do not represent the start of an allocation. Freeing such an interior pointer would cause undefined behavior. Comparison is also restricted to prevent reliance on pointer identity for owned values.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_typecheck_invalid_owned_binOp]

errors.message_template: invalid operands to unary expression (%0)
errors.cause: A unary operator (such as `++`, `--`, or unary `-`) was applied to an `_Owned` pointer. Incrementing or decrementing an `_Owned` pointer would change it to point to an interior location within (or outside) the allocation, making it impossible to correctly free the memory. BSC prohibits any unary operation that would alter the value of an `_Owned` pointer away from the original allocation address.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_typecheck_invalid_owned_unaOp]

errors.message_template: _Owned pointer type (%0) do not support ArraySubscript operate
errors.cause: The array subscript operator (`[]`) was applied to an `_Owned` pointer. In C, `p[i]` is equivalent to `*(p + i)`, which involves pointer arithmetic. Since `_Owned` pointers must always point to the exact start of their allocation, array subscript operations are not allowed on them. This restriction prevents the creation of interior pointers that cannot be correctly freed.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_typecheck_invalid_owned_arrsub]

errors.message_template: cannot assign to `%0` because it is borrowed
errors.cause:
You attempted to write to a variable while an outstanding borrow (via a `_Borrow`
pointer) still exists. The borrow guarantees the pointed-to value will not change
for the lifetime of the borrow. Assigning through the original name would violate
that guarantee and could cause the borrower to observe unexpected mutations.

fix_strategies.description: End the borrow before assigning by limiting the scope of the borrow pointer.
Restructure code so that the assignment occurs before the borrow is created.

errors.message_template: cannot move out of `%0` because it is borrowed
errors.cause:
Moving an `_Owned` value transfers ownership and invalidates the source. If any
borrow exists that points into that value, the move would leave the borrow dangling.
BSC prohibits moves while any borrow (mutable or immutable) is active on the value.

fix_strategies.description: End the borrow before the move.
Clone / copy the value instead of moving it, if applicable.

errors.message_template: cannot use `%0` because it was mutably borrowed
errors.cause:
While a mutable borrow is active, the original variable cannot be read through its
original path. A mutable borrow grants exclusive access to the borrower; allowing
reads through the original name would break this exclusivity and could lead to
observing partially updated state.

fix_strategies.description: Read the value through the mutable borrow pointer instead.
End the mutable borrow before reading the original variable.

errors.message_template: cannot borrow `%0` as mutable more than once at a time
errors.cause:
BSC enforces that only one mutable borrow of a given value can exist at any time.
Multiple mutable borrows would allow aliased mutation, which can cause data races
in concurrent code and undefined behavior even in single-threaded code.

fix_strategies.description: Use a single mutable borrow and pass it to the code that needs it.
End the first mutable borrow before creating the second.

errors.message_template: cannot borrow `%0` as immutable because it is also borrowed as mutable
errors.cause:
You cannot create an immutable borrow while a mutable borrow of the same value
exists. The mutable borrow has exclusive access; an immutable borrow would allow
observing the value through a second path, violating exclusivity.

fix_strategies.description: End the mutable borrow before creating the immutable borrow.
Use only one kind of borrow at a time.

errors.message_template: cannot borrow `%0` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable

fix_strategies.description: End all immutable borrows before creating a mutable borrow.
Restructure code to separate read and write phases.

errors.message_template: cannot return reference to local variable `%0`
errors.cause:
Local variables are destroyed when the function returns. Returning a `_Borrow`
pointer to a local variable would create a dangling pointer: the caller would
receive a reference to memory that is no longer valid. BSC detects this at compile
time and rejects it.

fix_strategies.description: Return an `_Owned` pointer to heap-allocated memory instead.
Pass the result through an output parameter that the caller owns.
Return the value by copy (non-pointer) when possible.

errors.message_template: `%0` does not live long enough
errors.cause:
The borrowed value goes out of scope while the borrow is still active. The borrow
pointer would become dangling because the value it references has been destroyed.
This commonly happens when an inner-scope variable is borrowed and the borrow
escapes to an outer scope.

fix_strategies.description: Extend the lifetime of the borrowed variable so it outlives the borrow.
Move the borrow usage into the same scope as the variable.

errors.message_template: borrow pointer variable '%0' lives longer than target variable
errors.cause:
The `_Borrow` pointer variable has a lifetime that extends beyond the lifetime of
the variable it borrows from. When the target variable is destroyed, the borrow
pointer becomes dangling. This is the legacy checker's equivalent of BSC-E0208.

fix_strategies.description: Ensure the target variable's scope encloses the borrow pointer's scope.
Declare the target variable in the same or an outer scope.

errors.message_template: There should be at most one mutable borrow targeting to '%0' at the same time
errors.cause:
This is the legacy checker's version of BSC-E0204. Two or more mutable `_Borrow`
pointers targeting the same variable exist simultaneously, which violates the
exclusivity rule for mutable borrows.

fix_strategies.description: Use only one mutable borrow at a time; end the first before creating the second.

errors.message_template: Return value cannot be a borrow from local variable '%0'
errors.cause:
This is the legacy checker's version of BSC-E0207. The function returns a `_Borrow`
pointer that references a local variable. Once the function returns, the local is
destroyed and the returned pointer is dangling.

fix_strategies.description: Return an `_Owned` pointer to heap-allocated memory.
Return by value instead of by reference.

errors.message_template: Can not modify '%0' because be borrowed
errors.cause:
This is the legacy checker's version of BSC-E0201. You attempted to modify a
variable while it is borrowed. The borrow guarantees the value will remain stable
for the duration of the borrow.

fix_strategies.description: End the borrow before modifying the variable.
Move the modification before the borrow is created.

errors.message_template: Can not read '%0' because be mut borrowed
errors.cause:
This is the legacy checker's version of BSC-E0203. While a mutable borrow is
active, reads through the original variable name are forbidden because the mutable
borrow has exclusive access.

fix_strategies.description: Read through the mutable borrow pointer instead of the original variable.
End the mutable borrow before reading the original variable.

errors.message_template: Can not use '%0' because expired
errors.cause:
The `_Borrow` pointer has expired -- the value it was borrowing from has gone out
of scope or has been moved. Using an expired borrow is equivalent to dereferencing
a dangling pointer, so BSC rejects it at compile time.

fix_strategies.description: Ensure the borrowed value outlives the borrow pointer.
Restructure scopes so the borrow is used while the target is still alive.

errors.message_template: %0 on a '_Borrow' qualified type is not allowed
errors.cause:
Certain qualifiers or operations cannot be applied to a type that is already
`_Borrow` qualified. For instance, applying `_Owned` on top of `_Borrow` is
contradictory: a pointer is either owning or borrowing, not both.

fix_strategies.description: Remove the conflicting qualifier. Decide whether the pointer should be `_Owned` or `_Borrow`.

errors.message_template: _Borrow type does not allow move ownership
errors.cause:
`_Borrow` pointers do not own the data they point to. You cannot transfer ownership
of a `_Borrow` pointer because there is no ownership to transfer. Only `_Owned`
pointers can be moved.

fix_strategies.description: Pass the borrow as a `_Borrow` parameter instead of an `_Owned` parameter.
If ownership transfer is needed, use an `_Owned` pointer from the start.

errors.message_template: incompatible borrow types, cannot cast %0 to %1
errors.cause:
You attempted to cast between pointer types whose `_Borrow` qualifications are
incompatible. BSC tracks borrow qualifiers as part of the type system and does
not allow implicit or explicit casts that would violate borrow safety.

fix_strategies.description: Avoid casting between `_Borrow` and `_Owned` types.
Redesign the code to use the correct qualifier from the start.

errors.message_template: incompatible borrow types, %0 and %1 cannot be compared
errors.cause:
You attempted to compare two pointers whose `_Borrow` qualifications are
incompatible. BSC disallows comparisons between pointers with mismatched borrow
qualifiers because such comparisons are semantically meaningless and usually
indicate a logic error.

fix_strategies.description: Compare pointers of the same borrow qualification.
Reconsider whether the comparison is logically correct.

errors.message_template: _Borrow type requires a pointer or reference (%0 is invalid)
errors.cause:
The `_Borrow` qualifier can only be applied to pointer types. Applying `_Borrow` to
a non-pointer type such as `int` or a struct value is invalid because borrowing is
a concept that applies to indirection -- a borrow is a reference to data owned
elsewhere.

fix_strategies.description: Apply `_Borrow` only to pointer types.
If you need a non-owning reference, use a pointer.

errors.message_template: no _Borrow qualified type found in the function parameters, the return type is not allowed to be _Borrow qualified
errors.cause:
A function that returns a `_Borrow` pointer must receive at least one `_Borrow`
parameter, because the returned borrow must refer to data that outlives the
function call. If no parameter is `_Borrow` qualified, the only possible source
for the returned borrow would be a local variable, which is always invalid.

fix_strategies.description: Add a `_Borrow` parameter that the return value can borrow from.
Change the return type to `_Owned` and transfer ownership instead.

errors.message_template: subscript of _Borrow pointer is not allowed
errors.cause:
`_Borrow` pointers represent a borrow of a single value, not an array. Array
subscript operations (`bp[i]`) on a `_Borrow` pointer are disallowed because BSC
cannot verify that the subscript stays within the bounds of valid memory. This
prevents out-of-bounds access through borrowed pointers.

fix_strategies.description: Access the value through simple dereference (`*bp`) instead of subscript.
If array access is needed, use a different pointer type with appropriate bounds guarantees.

errors.message_template: incompatible _Borrow function pointer types, cannot cast %0 to %1
errors.cause:
You attempted to cast between function pointer types that have different `_Borrow`
qualifications on their parameters or return types. BSC prevents this because
changing the borrow qualifier on a function pointer could lead to incorrect
lifetime tracking when the function is called through the cast pointer.

fix_strategies.description: Use function pointers with matching `_Borrow` qualifications.
Wrap the call in a new function with the correct signature.

errors.message_template: variable declarations of _Borrow qualified must be initialized
errors.cause:
A `_Borrow` pointer must always refer to valid data. An uninitialized `_Borrow`
variable would be a dangling reference from the start. BSC requires that every
`_Borrow` variable is initialized at the point of declaration to ensure it
immediately references valid memory.

fix_strategies.description: Initialize the `_Borrow` variable at declaration.

errors.message_template: the expression after '&_Mut' must be modifiable
errors.cause:
The `&_Mut` operator creates a mutable borrow, which allows writing to the
referenced value. The target expression must therefore be a modifiable lvalue.
Taking a mutable borrow of a `const` variable, a literal, or any other
non-modifiable expression is invalid.

fix_strategies.description: Use `&_Const` if you only need to read the value.
Remove the `const` qualifier if the variable should be mutable.

errors.message_template: '&_Mut' for function pointer is not allowed
errors.cause:
Function pointers refer to code, not data. Taking a mutable borrow of a function
pointer with `&_Mut` is meaningless because you cannot mutate a function's code
through a borrow. BSC prohibits this to prevent confusion and misuse.

fix_strategies.description: Use `&_Const` if you need a reference to the function pointer for reading.
Pass the function pointer by value instead.

errors.message_template: global or static variables are not allowed to be mutably borrowed within the safe zone
errors.cause:
Within a `_Safe` function or `_Safe` block, mutable borrows of global or static
variables are prohibited. Global and static variables can be accessed from multiple
threads or re-entrant calls; allowing mutable borrows in safe code would undermine
the data-race prevention that safe zones provide.

fix_strategies.description: Move the operation outside the safe zone.
Use atomic operations or synchronization primitives for thread-safe mutation.
Redesign the code to avoid mutable global state in safe contexts.

errors.message_template: cannot take mutable borrow of string literal with '&_Mut'; string literals are immutable
errors.cause:
String literals are stored in read-only memory and are inherently immutable. Taking
a mutable borrow with `&_Mut` on a string literal would imply the ability to
modify the string contents, which is undefined behavior. BSC rejects this at
compile time.

fix_strategies.description: Use `&_Const` for an immutable borrow of the string literal.
Copy the string into a mutable buffer if modification is needed.

errors.message_template: cannot take mutable borrow through string literal with '&_Mut *'; string literals are immutable
errors.cause:
Even when dereferencing a string literal pointer and then taking a mutable borrow
(`&_Mut *`), BSC still detects that the underlying data is a string literal and
rejects the operation. String literals are immutable regardless of how they are
accessed.

fix_strategies.description: Use `&_Const` for an immutable borrow.
Copy the string into a mutable buffer first.

errors.message_template: cannot pass string literal to parameter of type %0; string literals are immutable
errors.cause:
A function parameter expects a mutable `_Borrow` pointer, but you passed a string
literal. Since string literals are immutable, they cannot satisfy a mutable borrow
requirement. BSC catches this at the call site to prevent the function from
attempting to modify read-only memory.

fix_strategies.description: Copy the string literal into a mutable buffer and pass that instead.
Change the function signature to accept `const char *_Borrow` if it does not need mutation.

errors.message_template: %0 is forbidden in the safe zone
errors.cause: You performed an operation that BSC considers unsafe inside a `_Safe` function or block. Unsafe operations include raw pointer arithmetic, calling functions not marked `_Safe`, and certain type punning operations. These operations must be moved to an `_Unsafe` block.

fix_strategies.description: Wrap the unsafe operation in an `_Unsafe { }` block
Refactor to use safe alternatives

errors.message_template: %select{|'_Safe'|'_Unsafe'}0 can only appear before on function or statement or parenthesized expression
errors.cause: You placed `_Safe` or `_Unsafe` in a syntactically invalid position. These qualifiers can only appear on function declarations, before statements (as block qualifiers), or on parenthesized expressions.

fix_strategies.description: Move the qualifier to a valid position (function declaration or block statement)

example.bad_code: int _Safe x = 5;  // ERROR: _Safe can only appear on function or statement

errors.message_template: access to union field is _Unsafe and requires _Unsafe block
errors.cause: Accessing a union member is inherently unsafe because unions allow type punning — reading a member that wasn't the last one written is undefined behavior. BSC requires union field access to be wrapped in an `_Unsafe` block.

fix_strategies.description: Wrap the union access in an `_Unsafe` block

errors.message_template: conversion from type %0 to %1 is forbidden in the safe zone
errors.cause: You performed an explicit type cast that BSC considers unsafe inside a safe zone. This includes casts between incompatible pointer types, pointer-to-integer casts, and other conversions that could violate type safety or memory safety.

fix_strategies.description: Wrap the cast in an `_Unsafe` block
Use a safer alternative (e.g., pass the correct pointer type)

errors.message_template: implicit conversion from type %0 to %1 is forbidden in the safe zone; please use explicit cast or other means instead
errors.cause: An implicit type conversion that BSC considers unsafe occurred in a safe zone. Unlike BSC-E0304, this happens without an explicit cast — the compiler would normally perform the conversion silently, but BSC flags it because the conversion could violate safety guarantees.

fix_strategies.description: Use an explicit cast inside an `_Unsafe` block
Change the function signature to accept the correct type

errors.message_template: conversion from type %0 to %1 is forbidden
errors.cause: You attempted to convert between incompatible function pointer types. This is dangerous because calling a function through a pointer with the wrong signature is undefined behavior. BSC blocks this even when not explicitly in a safe zone for function pointer assignments.

fix_strategies.description: Ensure function pointer types match exactly
Wrap in `_Unsafe` if the conversion is intentional and correct

errors.message_template: %0 is forbidden in the _Safe function
errors.cause: You performed a specific operation that is not allowed in a `_Safe` function. This is similar to BSC-E0301 but specifically targets function-level restrictions. Operations like inline assembly, `goto`, or calling `_Unsafe` functions are forbidden.

fix_strategies.description: Move the operation to an `_Unsafe` block within the function
Extract the unsafe operation into a separate non-safe function

errors.message_template: defining mutable global variables is not allowed within the safe zone
errors.cause: Mutable global variables are a source of data races in concurrent programs. BSC's safe zone prohibits defining new mutable global variables. Constant globals are still allowed.

fix_strategies.description: Make the global `const` if it doesn't need to change
Define the global outside the safe zone

example.good_code:
const int global_max = 100;  // OK: const global

int global_counter = 0;  // OK: outside safe zone

errors.message_template: result of '++' or '--' cannot be used as return value in safe zone; move the increment/decrement out of the return statement (or add an explicit cast to void to suppress)
errors.cause: In BSC's safe zone, prefix/postfix `++` and `--` operators on pointers produce `void` to prevent pointer arithmetic mistakes. Returning this void result is an error.

fix_strategies.description: Separate the increment from the return statement

errors.message_template: generic function %0 cannot have both _Safe and _Unsafe declarations
errors.cause: A generic function was declared with both `_Safe` and `_Unsafe` variants, which is not allowed. Generic functions must have a single safety qualification.

fix_strategies.description: Choose one safety qualification for the generic function
If both variants are needed, use different function names

example.bad_code:
_Safe void process<T>(T *p);
_Unsafe void process<T>(T *p);  // ERROR: cannot have both

errors.message_template: function %0 has incompatible _Safe and _Unsafe declarations
errors.cause: A function has both `_Safe` and `_Unsafe` overloads, but their signatures are incompatible beyond the safety qualifier.

fix_strategies.description: Ensure the `_Safe` and `_Unsafe` declarations have compatible parameter and return types

errors.message_template: no matching function for call to %0; argument types do not match any _Safe or _Unsafe declaration
errors.cause: You called a function that has `_Safe`/`_Unsafe` overloads, but the provided arguments don't match any of the declared variants.

fix_strategies.description: Check the function's declared parameter types for both the `_Safe` and `_Unsafe` variants
Adjust argument types to match one of the declarations

errors.message_template: nullable pointer cannot be dereferenced
errors.cause: You attempted to dereference a pointer that is `_Nullable` — meaning it could be `NULL`. Dereferencing a null pointer is undefined behavior. BSC requires an explicit null check before dereferencing any nullable pointer.

fix_strategies.description: Add a null check before dereferencing
If you know the pointer is never null in this context, cast it to `_Nonnull`

errors.message_template: cannot pass nullable pointer argument
errors.cause: A function parameter expects a `_Nonnull` pointer, but you are passing a `_Nullable` pointer. The callee assumes the pointer is valid and may dereference it without checking.

fix_strategies.description: Add a null check before the call
If the pointer is known non-null, annotate it as `_Nonnull`

errors.message_template: cannot return nullable pointer type
errors.cause: The function's return type is `_Nonnull`, but you are returning a `_Nullable` pointer. Callers of this function expect a valid pointer and won't check for null.

fix_strategies.description: Add a null check and provide a fallback or early return
Change the return type to `_Nullable` if null is a valid return value

errors.message_template: cannot cast nullable pointer to nonnull type
errors.cause: You are explicitly casting a `_Nullable` pointer to a `_Nonnull` type without first establishing that the pointer is non-null. This bypasses the safety guarantee.

fix_strategies.description: Check for null before casting
Use a conditional assignment

errors.message_template: cannot access member through nullable pointer
errors.cause: You tried to access a struct member through a `_Nullable` pointer using `->`. If the pointer is null, this would be undefined behavior. A null check is required first.

fix_strategies.description: Add a null check before member access

errors.message_template: nonnull pointer cannot be assigned by nullable pointer
errors.cause: You are assigning a `_Nullable` pointer to a `_Nonnull` variable. This would allow a potentially null value to enter a non-null context, violating the nullability contract.

fix_strategies.description: Guard with a null check before assignment
Change the target type to `_Nullable` if null is acceptable

errors.message_template: `%0` is a _Nonnull pointer and must be properly initialized.
errors.cause: A `_Nonnull` pointer variable was declared without initialization. Since `_Nonnull` guarantees the pointer is always valid, it must be given a valid value at declaration time. An uninitialized `_Nonnull` pointer could be null or contain garbage.

fix_strategies.description: Initialize the pointer at declaration
If the value isn't available yet, use `_Nullable` instead

errors.message_template: %0 must be defined before it can be used
errors.cause: You referenced a trait that has not been defined yet. Traits must be declared with `_Trait` before they can be used in `_Impl` blocks or as pointer types.

fix_strategies.description: Define the trait before using it

example.bad_code: _Impl Printable for int { /* ... */ }  // ERROR: Printable not defined

errors.message_template: expected a pointer type which has implemented %0, found %1
errors.cause: You assigned a pointer to a trait pointer variable, but the pointed-to type has not implemented the required trait. The type must have an `_Impl` block for that trait.

fix_strategies.description: Add an `_Impl` block for the trait

errors.message_template: function %0 in %1 is not implemented for %2
errors.cause: Your `_Impl` block is missing one or more functions declared in the trait. All trait functions must be implemented.

fix_strategies.description: Implement all functions declared in the trait

errors.message_template: type of %0 conflicts with that of %1
errors.cause: The function you provided in your `_Impl` block has a different signature (parameter types or return type) than what the trait declares. The signatures must match exactly (except `This` is replaced with the concrete type).

fix_strategies.description: Match the function signature exactly as declared in the trait, substituting the concrete type for `This`

errors.message_template: only function declarations can be _Trait member
errors.cause: You declared something other than a function inside a `_Trait` block. Traits can only contain function declarations.

fix_strategies.description: Only declare functions in traits; use struct fields for data

errors.message_template: cannot _Impl _Trait for an instantiated type
errors.cause: You tried to implement a trait for an already-instantiated generic type. Trait implementations must be for base types, not specific generic instantiations.

fix_strategies.description: Implement the trait for the base (non-instantiated) type

errors.message_template: only _Trait pointer type is allowed to be declared
errors.cause: You tried to declare a trait variable that is not a pointer. Trait types can only be used as pointer types (`_Trait Name *`) because traits are dynamically dispatched and require indirection.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_variables_not_trait_pointer]

example.bad_code: _Trait Printable p;  // ERROR: only trait pointer type is allowed
example.good_code: _Trait Printable *p;  // OK: trait pointer

errors.message_template: the first parameter of _Trait member function must be 'This* this'
errors.cause: Trait member functions must take `This *this` as their first parameter. `This` is a placeholder for the implementing type.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for invalid_param_for_trait_member]

errors.message_template: unexpected token for ImplTraitDecl
errors.cause: The `_Impl` declaration has a syntax error. The expected syntax is `_Impl TraitName for TypeName { ... }`.

fix_strategies.description: Check the `_Impl` syntax: `_Impl <Trait> for <Type> { <functions> };`

errors.message_template: expected identifier after _Trait
errors.cause: The `_Trait` keyword must be followed by an identifier (the trait name).

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_expected_identifier_after_trait]

errors.message_template: _Trait is only allowed to be defined at top-level
errors.cause: Traits must be defined at file scope, not inside functions or other blocks.

fix_strategies.description: Move the trait definition to the top level of the file

errors.message_template: invalid syntax, semi not expected after '_Trait %0'
errors.cause: A semicolon was found immediately after `_Trait Name` instead of an opening brace. Trait definitions require a body.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_invalid_trait]

errors.message_template: %0 cannot directly call functions
errors.cause: You tried to call a function directly on a multi-trait pointer. Multi-trait pointers require disambiguation when calling trait functions.

fix_strategies.description: Cast to a specific trait pointer before calling the function

errors.message_template: must ignore '_Owned struct' tag before struct name
errors.cause: When referring to an `_Owned struct` type after its declaration, you should not prefix it with `struct`. The `_Owned struct Name { ... }` declaration introduces `Name` as a type name directly.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_tag_name]

example.bad_code:
_Owned struct Foo { _Public: int *_Owned p; };

void f(struct Foo *p) {}  // ERROR: must ignore '_Owned struct' tag
example.good_code: void f(Foo *p) {}  // OK: use Foo directly, not struct Foo

errors.message_template: inconsistent tag before struct name
errors.cause: You used an inconsistent tag (e.g., `struct` vs no tag) when referring to an `_Owned struct` type across different declarations.

fix_strategies.description: Use the type name consistently without the `struct` prefix for `_Owned struct` types

errors.message_template: need explicit constructor because %0 has private field
errors.cause: The `_Owned struct` has `_Private` fields, so it cannot be initialized with a designated initializer (`{ .field = value }`). You must provide an explicit constructor function.

fix_strategies.description: Create a constructor function that initializes the struct

errors.message_template: struct member cannot be redeclared
errors.cause: You declared the same member name more than once in an `_Owned struct`.

fix_strategies.description: Remove the duplicate member declaration

errors.message_template: invalid implicit use of member %0 in struct member function
errors.cause: You used a member name without explicitly accessing it through `this->` in a member function. BSC requires explicit member access via `this` pointer.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_invalid_member_use_in_class_method]

errors.message_template: function declared in struct scope cannot have 'static' storage class
errors.cause: Member functions of `_Owned struct` cannot be declared `static`. Use a regular (non-member) function if you need a static function.

fix_strategies.description: Remove the `static` keyword from the member function

errors.message_template: destructor %0 cannot be called directly
errors.cause: Destructors are called automatically when an `_Owned struct` variable goes out of scope. You cannot invoke them manually.

fix_strategies.description: Let the destructor run automatically at scope end
If you need early cleanup, use a block scope

errors.message_template: 'this' cannot be moved in destructor
errors.cause: Inside a destructor, the `this` pointer represents the object being destroyed. Moving `this` to another variable would transfer ownership away from the destruction process, leaving the object in an invalid state.

fix_strategies.description: Don't move `this` in the destructor; only free the owned fields

errors.message_template: expected the _Owned struct name after '~' to name the enclosing _Owned struct
errors.cause: The name after `~` in a destructor declaration doesn't match the struct name. Destructors must be named `~StructName`.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_owned_struct_destructor_name]

errors.message_template: destructor must have a function body
errors.cause: You declared a destructor without providing a function body. Destructors cannot be forward-declared; they must be defined with a body.

fix_strategies.description: Provide a function body that frees all `_Owned` fields

errors.message_template: the parameter of destructor must be '%0 this'
errors.cause: The destructor's parameter must be a pointer to the struct type, named `this`.

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for invalid_param_for_destructor]

example.bad_code: void ~Foo(Foo *this) { /* ... */ }  // OK

errors.message_template: destructor can only have one parameter
errors.cause: Destructors take exactly one parameter: `StructName *this`. Additional parameters are not allowed.

fix_strategies.description: Remove extra parameters; if you need additional cleanup logic, call helper functions from within the destructor

errors.message_template: incompatible conversion from pointer type '%0' to non-pointer type '%1' in member function call
errors.cause: A member function call involves passing a pointer type where a non-pointer type is expected, or vice versa. The `this` parameter or other parameters have a type mismatch involving pointer indirection.

fix_strategies.description: Check the member function's parameter types and ensure the object/arguments match
If calling `obj.method()`, ensure `obj` has the correct pointer indirection level

errors.message_template: incompatible conversion from const type '%0' to non-const type '%1' in member function call
errors.cause: You are calling a non-const member function on a const-qualified object. The function expects a mutable `this` pointer but received a `const` one.

fix_strategies.description: Call only const-compatible member functions on const objects
Remove the `const` qualifier if mutation is intended

errors.message_template: incompatible conversion from non _Owned type '%0' to _Owned type '%1' in member function call
errors.cause: A member function expects an `_Owned` pointer parameter, but you passed a non-owned (raw or `_Borrow`) pointer. Ownership cannot be implicitly created — it must be explicitly transferred.

fix_strategies.description: Pass an `_Owned` pointer to the function
If the function needs to consume ownership, ensure the caller has ownership to give

errors.message_template: type of member function is wrong, CVR qualified type is unsupported, but found '%0'
errors.cause: The member function's type uses a const/volatile/restrict (CVR) qualified type in a position where BSC does not support it. BSC member functions have specific rules about where qualifiers can appear.

fix_strategies.description: Remove unsupported CVR qualifiers from the member function's type

errors.message_template: type of parameter 'this' is wrong, expected 'This*' or 'This' or '%0*' or '%0', but found '%1'
errors.cause: The `this` parameter in a member function has an incorrect type. It must be either a pointer to the struct type (`Type *this`) or the struct type itself (`Type this`).

fix_strategies.description: [TODO: Document fix for err_this_type_unsupported]

errors.message_template: '_Async' can only appear on functions
errors.cause: The `_Async` qualifier was applied to something other than a function declaration. Only functions can be asynchronous.

fix_strategies.description: Move `_Async` to a function declaration

example.bad_code: _Async void fetch_data() { /* ... */ }  // OK

errors.message_template: 'main' is not allowed to be declared _Async
errors.cause: The `main` function cannot be `_Async` because it is the program entry point and has a fixed calling convention defined by the C runtime.

fix_strategies.description: Create a separate `_Async` function and call it from `main`

errors.message_template: _Await expression is not allowed to appear in %0
errors.cause: `_Await` was used in a context where it is not valid, such as inside a non-async function, a global initializer, or certain control flow constructs.

fix_strategies.description: Use `_Await` only inside `_Async` functions

errors.message_template: _Async function does not support %0
errors.cause: Certain language features are not supported inside `_Async` functions due to the coroutine transformation. This may include specific control flow constructs or variable-length arrays.

fix_strategies.description: Refactor the unsupported feature out of the `_Async` function
Move the unsupported operation into a synchronous helper function

errors.message_template: the _Await expression's external function declaration must be modified by _Async or return 'Future' type
errors.cause: `_Await` can only be applied to calls that return a `Future` type or to functions declared `_Async`. The expression you tried to await does not meet either condition.

fix_strategies.description: Make the called function `_Async`, or
Ensure it returns a `Future` type

errors.message_template: '%0' was not found, you need to include %1 before using the '_Async' keyword
errors.cause: The `_Async` runtime requires certain support functions to be declared. You are missing the necessary header include.

fix_strategies.description: Include the required header as specified in the error message

errors.message_template: _Await expression was not found in _Async function
errors.cause: An `_Async` function must contain at least one `_Await` expression. A function declared `_Async` without any awaits should be a regular function instead.

fix_strategies.description: Add an `_Await` expression, or
Remove the `_Async` qualifier if the function doesn't need to be asynchronous

errors.message_template: function which returns 'Future' type should not be modified by '_Async'
errors.cause: A function that already returns a `Future` type should not also be marked `_Async`. The `_Async` qualifier automatically wraps the return type in `Future`; applying both would result in double-wrapping.

fix_strategies.description: Remove `_Async` if you explicitly return `Future`
Or remove the `Future` return type and let `_Async` handle it

errors.message_template: struct definition in generic fuction is not supported in BSC
errors.cause: BSC does not allow defining new struct types inside generic functions. Struct definitions must be at file scope or inside non-generic functions.

fix_strategies.description: Move the struct definition outside the generic function

errors.message_template: extended type of a BSC member function cannot be an instantiated type
errors.cause: When declaring a member function for a generic type, you cannot use an instantiated (concrete) type as the extended type. Use the uninstantiated generic form instead.

fix_strategies.description: Use the generic type form, not a specific instantiation

errors.message_template: conflicting function declarations for %0
errors.cause: Multiple declarations of the same function have incompatible signatures. This often happens with generic function specializations or overloads that create ambiguity.

fix_strategies.description: Ensure all declarations of the same function have matching signatures
Remove or rename conflicting declarations

errors.message_template: extended type of a BSC member function cannot be a generic typealias
errors.cause: Member functions cannot be defined for generic type aliases. They must be defined for the actual type.

fix_strategies.description: Define the member function on the concrete type, not the typealias

errors.message_template: BSC generic typealias cannot be declared within a function
errors.cause: Generic type aliases must be declared at file scope, not inside function bodies.

fix_strategies.description: Move the generic typealias to file scope

errors.message_template: BSC constexpr function does not support %0
errors.cause: BSC's `constexpr` functions are evaluated at compile time and support only a limited subset of operations. Features like dynamic allocation, I/O, and certain control flow are not available.

fix_strategies.description: Remove the unsupported feature from the constexpr function
If the feature is necessary, make the function a regular (non-constexpr) function

errors.message_template: BSC constexpr function does not support type %0
errors.cause: The type used in a constexpr function is not supported for compile-time evaluation. Only simple types (integers, floats, etc.) are supported in constexpr contexts.

fix_strategies.description: Use a supported type, or make the function non-constexpr

errors.message_template: BSC constexpr variable does not support type %0
errors.cause: A `constexpr` variable was declared with a type that cannot be evaluated at compile time.

fix_strategies.description: Use a compile-time-compatible type (e.g., `int`, `float`, `char`)

errors.message_template: BSC constexpr if condition expression does not support type %0
errors.cause: The condition in a `constexpr if` statement uses a type that cannot be evaluated at compile time. The condition must be a compile-time constant of a supported type.

fix_strategies.description: Ensure the condition is a compile-time integer or boolean expression

errors.message_template: no instance member named %0 in %1; did you mean to use '::' instead of '%select{.|->}2'?
errors.cause: You used `.` or `->` to access a member that doesn't exist as an instance member of the type. It may be a static/type-level function that should be called with `::` instead.

fix_strategies.description: Use `::` for type-level (static) functions
Use `.` or `->` only for instance members

errors.message_template: (EnhanceC) %0 attribute applied to function with more than one pointer arguments, please specify the index argument in the %0 attribute
errors.cause: A BSC attribute was applied to a function that has multiple pointer parameters, but the attribute doesn't specify which pointer it applies to. When there is ambiguity, you must use the index argument.

fix_strategies.description: Specify the pointer index in the attribute to disambiguate

errors.message_template: (EnhanceC) %0 attribute: The number of pointer arguments index cannot be zero
errors.cause: The pointer index argument in a BSC attribute is 1-based. Passing `0` as the index is invalid.

fix_strategies.description: Use index `1` for the first pointer parameter, `2` for the second, etc.

errors.message_template: function unsupport overload
errors.cause: The function you are trying to overload does not support operator overloading. Only specific operator functions can be overloaded in BSC.

fix_strategies.description: Check that you are overloading a supported operator

errors.message_template: unsupported operator type
errors.cause: The operator type you are trying to overload is not supported by BSC. BSC supports overloading for a specific set of operators (arithmetic, comparison, etc.).

fix_strategies.description: Use a supported operator type for overloading

errors.message_template: overloaded function %0 first parameter or return type must be struct or enumeration pointer type
